lines: A clocked kick and bass voice for psytrance: a pitch-swept sine kick on each beat, a filtered saw bass on the sixteenths between them, and ramp and gate outputs spanning a sixteen-bar cycle
Sets the pitch the kick sweep ends on, in twelve semitone steps from C1 up to C2
Sets the pitch the kick sweep starts from, in thirty-six semitone steps from C6 up to C9
Moves the first control point of the kick's pitch curve along in time, holding the sweep near its top for longer at the start of each kick
Raises the first control point of the kick's pitch curve, making the fall from the SWEEP pitch down to the PITCH pitch more gradual
Sets the bass note, in twelve semitone steps from C1 up to B1, before the V/OCT input transposes it
Scales the level of the first bass note after each kick; the other bass notes play at full level
Chooses one of five saw shapes for the bass oscillator
Warps the saw shape chosen by SAW, sweeping the shaping factor of whichever shape is selected
Transposes the bass, one octave per volt over -4V to 4V, and leaves the kick pitch alone
The clock, one pulse per bar; the time between pulses is divided into sixteen steps, and nothing sounds until two pulses have arrived
A trigger restarts the kick's pitch envelope and holds the bass silent until the next quarter note
A ramp falling from 8V to 0V across the first fifteen bars of the sixteen-bar cycle, then holding at 0V for the last one
A ramp rising from 0V to 8V across the sixteen-bar cycle
8V through the sixteenth bar of the cycle and 0V through the other fifteen
The kick drum, a sine sweeping down from the SWEEP pitch to the PITCH pitch, at 5V peak
The bass, a saw through a four-pole low-pass whose cutoff falls across each sixteenth note
Note — the bass plays on the second, third and fourth sixteenth of each quarter note, leaving the first of the four to the kick
Note — the module is silent until a clock is patched to BAR and two pulses have arrived; it takes all of its timing, one bar per pulse, from that clock and produces nothing without it
kickbaba.notes: No control on this module carries a configParam name, so an untagged control would show nothing at all. The panel names differ from the code's names for three controls: the knob printed SWEEP is kickPitchMax, the knob printed ROLL is bassVelocity, and the jack printed BAR is the clock input. The four text readouts and the bass waveform graph are Label and draw() artwork, not parameters, so they cannot be clicked.

lines: A through-zero FM oscillator pair at a fixed tuning: a modulator and a carrier, with the through-zero result spread across a stereo pair
Sets the root note, -12 to 12 semitones from C, and the readout names it
Detunes the two stereo outputs in opposite directions, by up to about 0.8Hz each at maximum
Sets how far the modulator drives the carrier frequency, 0 to 100 percent
Chooses the modulator waveform from sine, triangle, saw, ramp, square, band-limited saw and band-limited square
Chooses the waveform used by the carrier and by both stereo outputs, from sine, triangle, saw, ramp, square, band-limited saw and band-limited square
Transposes the modulator by whole octaves, -4 to 4, with 0 putting it at C3 while KEY is at C
Transposes the carrier and both stereo outputs by whole octaves, -4 to 4, with 0 putting the stereo pair at C4 while KEY is at C
Scales the modulation amount set by the knob, 0V shutting the modulation off and 10V leaving the knob setting untouched
The modulator on its own, -5V to 5V, at the pitch that drives the through-zero modulation
The carrier waveform on its own, -5V to 5V, running five octaves below the pitch of the two stereo outputs at the same settings
The left channel of the through-zero result, -5V to 5V; its oscillator is advanced twice per sample, so this channel sounds an octave above the carrier octave set on the panel
The right channel of the through-zero result, -5V to 5V, mixing the right oscillator detuned by STEREO with the left channel's oscillator
tzfmlead.notes: Two things in the code need a person to settle, and both are stated in the lines above because the reader can hear them. First, the jack printed CAR runs at mtof(carrierOctave*12 + root), which is MIDI note 0 at the default octave, while the through-zero outputs run from C4 at the same setting, a fixed five octaves apart. Second, the centre oscillator oscFmCenter is never processed: the code reads oscFmLeft twice per sample and calls the first read 'center', so the left oscillator advances at double rate and both stereo outputs carry it. Whether either is intended is a question for the maker.
